root_idea.summary: The root centers on intensity and force; in its dominant emotional branch, غضب denotes intensified displeasure directed toward resistance or retaliation.
root_idea.development: The lexical tradition connects the sense of firmness or hardness with the intensification of displeasure into anger. In divine usage, this develops into punitive disapproval or retribution, while related derivatives extend to forceful, severe, and hard qualities.

senses.definition: To be or become angry with someone.
senses.usage_conditions: The ordinary verb takes the person or object of anger in constructions such as غَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ. Quranic usage includes both human and divine subjects; the divine usage is specified separately below.

senses.definition: Of God, to direct punitive wrath against someone—to express disapproval of disobedience with punishment as its consequence.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the Quranic theological use of the verb when God is the subject; it does not describe a human physiological emotion.

senses.definition: Anger or wrath as an intense state of displeasure, conventionally associated with a drive toward retaliation.
senses.usage_conditions: In ordinary human usage, the word denotes an emotional state. Classical definitions distinguish anger from grief and describe both commendable anger for truth and blameworthy anger in a wrongful cause.

senses.definition: Divine punitive wrath: disapproval of disobedience expressed as retribution.
senses.usage_conditions: When attributed to God, the Quranic usage is interpreted as punitive consequence rather than a human-like physiological state.
An epithet for an angry person; some Classical descriptions add the nuance of being quick or readily angered. The Quranic occurrences describe Moses in this state.

senses.definition: Subjected to anger; one who has incurred divine punitive wrath.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic expression الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ is a passive-participial construction. Its traditional interpretation identifies the referent as the Jews, but that identification is an interpretation of the referent rather than the lexical meaning of the participle itself.

senses.definition: Departing in anger or enmity, breaking off or quitting one's people.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction ذهب مُغَاضِبًا, the active participle describes departure accompanied by estrangement or anger, rather than merely the internal state of being angry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In Classical constructions, غَضِبَ لَهُ means to be angry on behalf of a living person, while غَضِبَ بِهِ is used when that person is dead; غَضِبَ فِي اللهِ means to be angry for God's sake, and غَضِبَ مِنْ لَا شَيْءٍ means to become angry without cause.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are constructional and contextual distinctions of the Form I verb, not separate Quranic meanings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a mare, to champ or snap at the bit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized animal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be afflicted with the disease called غُضَاب.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-form medical usage; the same disease is also reported of the eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make one another angry; to engage in reciprocal anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III reciprocal usage, distinct from the Quranic active-participial construction of departure in anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To anger someone or make someone angry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative Form IV usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become angry, or to become angry progressively after having been somewhat angry already.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V usage with an inchoative or intensifying nuance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a cooking pot, to boil fiercely over its contents.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or tropical Form V usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intensely or densely red; thick or dense in quality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially in descriptions of a deep, intense red.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hard rock fixed in a mountain and distinct from it; also a hard, rounded rock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete geological noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lion; also a bull.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Separate animal-noun usages of the same headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An eminence or raised protuberance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical elevation, including an eminence of the kind called أَكَمَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fleshly protuberance above or beneath the eye, including a flatulent swelling of the eyelid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shield-like object made from camel hide, with one part folded over another; also a camel-hide fighting garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specialized equipment and clothing made from hide.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The skin or hide of an aged mountain goat, a fish, the head, or the part between a bull's horns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A group of specialized hide terms reported under the same headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A patch or area of smallpox on the skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A medical usage describing skin covered in a smallpox patch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The irascible faculty or anger-producing power.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical philosophical or psychological expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Motes or specks in the eye or eyes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An ocular medical usage; the variant غُضَابٌ is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease or skin eruption, reported variously as distinct from or including smallpox.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources preserve variation about whether the term denotes an eruption generally or smallpox specifically.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stern or austere in look or countenance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported especially of a woman or a she-camel, as explicitly specified in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company or group of women.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective-noun usage distinct from the adjective meaning stern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A malignant serpent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man perturbed or difficult in social intercourse and comportment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjective describing social manner and conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An anatomical region between the penis and an adjacent structure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term whose second anatomical reference is not further identified in the supplied evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Afflicted with the disease called غِضَاب, especially smallpox.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized medical use of the passive participle, separate from مَغْضُوبٌ عَلَيْهِ meaning one subjected to anger.

cautions: The public headword مُغَاضِب is presented as a Form III active participle because the Quranic occurrence is participial, while the associated Classical verb is غَاضَبَ.
The traditional identification of الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ with the Jews is preserved as a referential interpretation, not as a restriction in the lexical definition.
